# Views

A view is a markdown file that attn draws in a tile. It holds prose and parts. A part opens with `:::name` and its arguments on a line of their own, and closes with a line that holds only `:::`. A part that holds other parts opens with four colons and closes with `::::`. Put an argument's value in quotes when it holds a space, as in `run="scripts/weather.sh Stockholm"`.

A view's data is what its `:::data` parts provide. In a part, `{field}` is a value from that data, a field inside a field is written `{ci.state}`, and `{field|format}` draws the value in a format. In a list, a table or a four-colon part, `{field}` is a field of each item.

This is language version 1. When attn keeps a view, it writes `<!-- attn-view 1 -->` on the view's first line. Do not write that line in a view for one task: a view without it is read as the current version.

Below, Keys are the keys the user presses on a part, and Reports is what the part adds to the answers the user sends back to the agent that opened the view.

When the user sends, attn writes the answers to `<view>.responses.json` beside the view and types one line into your conversation that sums them up and names the file. In the file, `path` names the view, `answers` holds the answers outside `::::each` and `::::one-by-one` by the question's name, and `rows` holds each item's answers by the item's `id`, or by its place from 1 when it has none. A choice is its label, a `question-multi` answer is a list of labels, and a written answer is its text. A `one-by-one` item also has a `verdict`: `kept`, `changed` when the user rewrote a `Value:` text, or `skipped`. Items the user never reached are left out. The user can send again, and the file then holds every answer so far.

## Parts

| Part | Written | Draws |
|---|---|---|
| markdown | `prose` | Prose, headings, links and code blocks, drawn as markdown. |
| media | `![label](file)` | A picture or an audio clip, chosen by the file's type. It stands on a line of its own. |
| tasks | `- [ ] text` | A task list drawn as checkboxes. |
| question | `:::question <name>` | A question with choices, written as in an ask: the question on the first line, then one `- [ ] choice` per line, and `Recommended:` if one choice is best. With no choices it takes text. |
| question-multi | `:::question-multi <name>` | A question where the user picks any number of choices. |
| question-text | `:::question-text <name>` | A question answered with text. `Value:` gives the text it starts with. |
| question-file | `:::question-file <name>` | A question answered with a file. |
| compare | `:::compare` | Two media lines side by side, or one flipped over the other. |
| data | `:::data` | Names one source of the view's values. It draws nothing. |
| status | `:::status <field>` | A state mark with its word. |
| facts | `:::facts` | Lines of label and value, one `label \| value` per line. |
| list | `:::list <items>` | One row per item, written as slots, one `slot: value` per line. |
| table | `:::table <items>` | One table line per item. The body is a markdown table whose one row is the template for each item. |
| chart | `:::chart <items> x=<field> y=<field>` | A line chart of the items. |
| each | `::::each <items>` | Its content once per item: prose, headings, media, questions and parts. |
| one-by-one | `::::one-by-one <items>` | One item at a time, with progress and a summary before sending. |
| entry | `:::entry <command>` | A line to type in. ↩ runs the command with the text. The body is the hint shown while the line is empty. |
| controls | `:::controls` | The view's own buttons, in its header, one command per line. |
| commands | `:::commands` | Defines the view's own commands, one `name: program arguments` per line. It draws nothing. |

Do not name a part `script`: attn reserves the name and refuses it.

## Example

```markdown
# Check 12 transcripts

::::one-by-one clips.jsonl
![{id}]({file})

:::question-text transcript
Is this what you said?
Value: {transcript}
:::
::::
```

## Where a view's values come from

Each `:::data` part names one source. A `:::data` part without `as=` puts its values at the top of the view's data, and with `as=` they appear under that field. Two parts cannot use the same field. A store's values appear under the store's name. The `data` section below lists the arguments.

Opening a view runs nothing. The tile names each command of `run=` and `:::commands`, and waits until the user presses `r` to start them. When a command line or the script it names changes, attn stops that command and waits for the user again.

attn's data sets, for `attn=`:

- `sessions`: the profile's sessions.
- `pull-requests`: the pull requests attn follows.
- `asks`: the open asks, and those answered in the last day.
- `seeds`: the open seeds.
- `app`: attn itself: its version and what is new.

The types of a store's fields:

- `text`: text.
- `number`: a number.
- `yes-no`: yes or no.

The formats, written `{field|format}`:

- `duration`: a number of seconds, drawn as a duration such as 1h 4m.
- `ago`: an instant, drawn as how long ago it was, such as 4 min ago.

## Commands a view can run

A row's `press:`, `controls:` and `group-controls:` slots, `:::controls` and `:::entry` name commands, such as `press: open`.

attn's commands:

- `open`: opens the row's session, pull request or file.
- `new-session`: starts a session.
- `choose-harness`: picks the harness of a new session.
- `unsnooze`: brings a snoozed session back.
- `approve`: approves a pull request.
- `merge`: merges a pull request.
- `mute`: mutes a pull request.
- `mute-author`: mutes a pull request's author.
- `mute-repo`: mutes a repository.
- `refresh`: fetches the data again.
- `follow`: follows the next turn; a switch that shows on or off.
- `settings`: opens Settings.
- `whats-new`: shows what is new in attn.

The commands of a view with a store, such as `press: toggle done` and `:::entry add text`:

- `add <field>`: adds an item with the typed text in the field.
- `set <field> <value>`: sets the row's field to the value.
- `toggle <field>`: switches the row's yes-no field.
- `remove`: removes the row.

A view defines its own commands in `:::commands`. Each is a program and its arguments, run in the view's folder and never through a shell. A view's own command cannot take the name of one of attn's commands or of a store's commands.

## markdown

`prose`

Prose, headings, links and code blocks, drawn as markdown.

````markdown
# Release checklist

Read the notes before you start. A **bold** word, a [link](https://example.com) and `code` draw as markdown.

```sh
attn open view.md
```
````

## media

`![label](file)`

A picture or an audio clip, chosen by the file's type. It stands on a line of its own.

Keys: Space plays and pauses a clip, ⇧← and ⇧→ move it 5 s.

```markdown
# The new icon

![The icon at 64 px](icon-64.png)

![How the name sounds](name.wav)
```

## tasks

`- [ ] text`

A task list drawn as checkboxes.

Keys: x checks.

Reports: which tasks are checked.

```markdown
# Before the release

- [x] Write the notes
- [ ] Tag the build
- [ ] Tell the team
```

## question

`:::question <name>`

A question with choices, written as in an ask: the question on the first line, then one `- [ ] choice` per line, and `Recommended:` if one choice is best. With no choices it takes text.

Arguments:

- `<name>`: the name the answer is saved under. Required.

Keys: digits pick.

Reports: the choice.

```markdown
:::question size
Which size should the icon be?
- [ ] 48 px
- [ ] 64 px — the size the dock uses
Recommended: 64 px
:::
```

## question-multi

`:::question-multi <name>`

A question where the user picks any number of choices.

Arguments:

- `<name>`: the name the answer is saved under. Required.

Keys: digits pick and unpick.

Reports: the choices.

```markdown
:::question-multi platforms
Which platforms does the release cover?
- [ ] macOS
- [ ] Linux
:::
```

## question-text

`:::question-text <name>`

A question answered with text. `Value:` gives the text it starts with.

Arguments:

- `<name>`: the name the answer is saved under. Required.

Keys: e or ↩ writes, Escape leaves the text.

Reports: the text, when it is not the `Value:` text.

```markdown
:::question-text title
What should the release be called?
Value: Autumn release
:::
```

## question-file

`:::question-file <name>`

A question answered with a file.

Arguments:

- `<name>`: the name the answer is saved under. Required.

Keys: ↩ picks a file.

Reports: the file's path.

```markdown
:::question-file screenshot
Which screenshot shows the problem?
:::
```

## compare

`:::compare`

Two media lines side by side, or one flipped over the other.

Keys: f flips.

```markdown
# Before and after

:::compare
![Before](before.png)
![After](after.png)
:::
```

## data

`:::data`

Names one source of the view's values. It draws nothing.

Arguments:

- `attn=<data set>`: one of attn's own data sets.
- `run=<program and arguments>`: a program and its arguments that prints one JSON object. attn runs it in the view's folder, never through a shell. Name the program by its name, such as `gh`, or from the view's folder, such as `scripts/status.sh`; attn notices a change to the files in the view's folder that the line names.
- `every=<duration>`: how often attn reruns `run`, such as 30s or 10m, and at most once a second. Without it, attn runs the command once each time the view is shown.
- `file=<file>`: a JSON or JSON Lines file in the view's folder.
- `store=<store>`: the name of a store: values a kept view owns. Its body lists the store's fields, one `name: type` per line, and its values appear under the store's name. `store="view/set"` shows another kept view's store and takes no body.
- `as=<field>`: the field the values appear under.

Keys: r reruns.

It goes at the top level of a view, not inside a four-colon part.

```markdown
:::data attn="sessions"
:::

:::data run="scripts/weather.sh Stockholm" every="10m" as="weather"
:::

:::data file="team.json" as="team"
:::
```

## status

`:::status <field>`

A state mark with its word.

Arguments:

- `<field>`: the field that holds the state. Required.

```markdown
:::data run="scripts/main-status.sh" every="30s"
:::

:::status ci.state
:::
```

## facts

`:::facts`

Lines of label and value, one `label | value` per line.

```markdown
:::data run="scripts/main-status.sh" every="30s"
:::

:::facts
Head | `{head.sha}` {head.subject} · {head.at|ago}
Landed today | {landed}
:::
```

## list

`:::list <items>`

One row per item, written as slots, one `slot: value` per line.

Arguments:

- `<items>`: the field that holds the items, or a .json or .jsonl file in the view's folder. Required.
- `foldable`: the heading above the list folds it.
- `count`: the heading above the list shows how many items it has.

Slots:

- `lead`: the mark at the start of the row.
- `title`: the row's main text.
- `sub`: a second, quieter line.
- `aside`: text at the end of the row.
- `press`: the command ↩ runs on the row.
- `controls`: the commands the row offers, separated by commas.
- `empty`: what the list says when it has no items.
- `group-aside`: text at the end of the heading above the list.
- `group-controls`: the commands the heading above the list offers, separated by commas.

Keys: j and k move, ↩ runs press.

Reports: the row's answers.

```markdown
:::data run="scripts/main-status.sh" every="30s"
:::

## CI on main

:::list ci.jobs foldable count
lead: {conclusion}
title: {name}
aside: {seconds|duration}
press: open
empty: No jobs ran.
:::
```

## table

`:::table <items>`

One table line per item. The body is a markdown table whose one row is the template for each item.

Arguments:

- `<items>`: the field that holds the items, or a .json or .jsonl file in the view's folder. Required.

Keys: j and k move.

```markdown
:::data run="scripts/landings.sh" every="1m"
:::

:::table landings
| Session | Change | Gate | Took |
|---|---|---|---|
| {session} | {subject} | {gate} | {seconds|duration} |
:::
```

## chart

`:::chart <items> x=<field> y=<field>`

A line chart of the items.

Arguments:

- `<items>`: the field that holds the items, or a .json or .jsonl file in the view's folder. Required.
- `x=<field>`: the item field along the bottom. Required.
- `y=<field>`: the item field up the side. Required.

```markdown
:::data run="scripts/weather.sh Stockholm" every="10m"
:::

:::chart hours x=hour y=temp
:::
```

## each

`::::each <items>`

Its content once per item: prose, headings, media, questions and parts.

Arguments:

- `<items>`: the field that holds the items, or a .json or .jsonl file in the view's folder. Required.

Reports: each item's answers.

```markdown
:::data attn="pull-requests"
:::

::::each repositories
## {name}

:::list pulls
title: {title}
aside: {checks}
controls: approve, merge
:::
::::
```

## one-by-one

`::::one-by-one <items>`

One item at a time, with progress and a summary before sending.

Arguments:

- `<items>`: the field that holds the items, or a .json or .jsonl file in the view's folder. Required.

Keys: ↩ keeps and goes on, s skips, ← and → step; e writes and digits pick in the item's questions.

Reports: each item's answers, and whether the user kept, changed or skipped it.

```markdown
# Pick the best take

::::one-by-one takes.jsonl
![{name}]({file})

:::question verdict
Is this take good enough?
- [ ] Keep
- [ ] Redo
:::
::::
```

## entry

`:::entry <command>`

A line to type in. ↩ runs the command with the text. The body is the hint shown while the line is empty.

Arguments:

- `<command>`: the command and its arguments. Required.

Keys: ↩ runs.

```markdown
:::commands
note: scripts/add-note.sh
:::

:::entry note
Write a note
:::
```

## controls

`:::controls`

The view's own buttons, in its header, one command per line.

Keys: each control's letter.

It goes at the top level of a view, not inside a four-colon part.

```markdown
:::controls
refresh
follow
:::
```

## commands

`:::commands`

Defines the view's own commands, one `name: program arguments` per line. It draws nothing.

It goes at the top level of a view, not inside a four-colon part.

```markdown
:::data run="scripts/main-status.sh" every="30s"
:::

:::commands
rerun: scripts/rerun.sh {id}
:::

:::list ci.jobs
title: {name}
controls: rerun
:::
```
